clue.text: Spinner Shane Warne's head aching: getting out with one maiden

indicators.note: the head of a name is its opening letter, so only the start of the bowler's surname is kept
letters getting out of their places scatter and can be set down again in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the cricketer's surname
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Leg-spinner Shane Warne, nursing a headache, is dismissed after bowling a maiden over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests Warne, the famous Australian spin bowler, but it is the definition. A maiden is an over in cricket from which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A washing machine spins clothes in its drum to wring out water, so it is jocularly a spinner.

clue.text: Fighter, eg wrestler (not small), stopped early with wound

indicators.note: not small says the abbreviation for small must be taken away
something stopped early never reaches its end, so its final letter goes
wound as the past of wind means twisted round, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before losing letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boxer, or perhaps a wrestler, is halted prematurely by an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: The wrestler loses its S and its last letter to give WRETLE, then everything from 'eg' to 'with' is rearranged; 'wound' is the twisting signal, not an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A welterweight is a boxer in the weight class between lightweight and middleweight, so a fighter.

clue.text: Extremely scared around brown bear

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters
around says one piece wraps about the other

blocks.note: the outside letters of the word
tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: Someone is terrified by a brown bear nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate it, as in 'I can't bear him' or 'I can't stand him'.

clue.text: Made-up cuties, men swell up

indicators.note: something made up is invented or fabricated, so the letters are composed afresh

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pretty girls in make-up make the men swoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made-up' reads as wearing cosmetics, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To intumesce is a technical verb for to enlarge or bulge, as tissue does when inflamed.

clue.text: Good style, with profiterole initially missing chocolate filling

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the pastry's name
missing says that letter is absent from the word

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
panache is flamboyant style
the first letter of the pastry

explanation.surface: A stylish dessert, but the profiterole lacks its chocolate filling.
explanation.walkthrough: Panache loses the P that begins profiterole, which itself belongs to the dessert scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganache is a smooth mix of chocolate and cream used to fill or coat cakes and pastries.

clue.text: Old-fashioned spies set up meeting with chief

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means raised so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: arch means chief, as in archenemy
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Outdated spooks arrange a meeting with their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' sounds like a sting or a staged meeting, but it turns the agency round.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means belonging to an earlier era, hence old-fashioned.

clue.text: Indicators of hours and seconds?

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hours
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: A question about what shows the time on a clock face.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue defines clock pointers; read as wordplay, it spells out the abbreviation for hours, the word 'and', and the one for seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: The hour and second hands on a clock are the pointers that indicate the time.

clue.text: Deputy close to Gordon Brown also in speech

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept
in speech means as said out loud, so the word is chosen for its sound

blocks.note: the final letter of the name
umber is a brown earth pigment
too means also, and sounds like the number

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown's deputy, close by, is also in the speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown, the former British prime minister, is split in two: his first name gives a letter and his surname a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A number two is someone's second-in-command, the person who deputises for the leader.

clue.text: Did rest with skinny latte in centre

indicators.note: what sits in the centre of a word is its middle letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: skinny and lean both mean thin
the middle letter of the five-letter coffee

explanation.surface: Someone takes a break with a skimmed-milk coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinny latte' reads as one coffee order, but skinny is a separate piece meaning thin.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean is to rest against something for support, and leant is its past tense, matching did rest.

clue.text: Tag and arrest somebody

blocks.note: to nick is British slang for to arrest
a somebody, a famous person, is a name

explanation.surface: A police officer marks a suspect and takes someone into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang the police nick, or arrest, a suspect; and a somebody or celebrity is a big name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag is an informal label for a person, which is exactly what a nickname is.

clue.text: Ungenerous or liberal: perhaps one does mind job in hospital?

definitions.text: perhaps one does mind job in hospital?

indicators.note: liberal means free and unconstrained, so the letters are freed to take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A political jibe: is someone mean or liberal, and do they mind working in a hospital?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' sits opposite 'Ungenerous' as if they were contrasting adjectives, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosurgeon operates on the brain, so their job, punningly, is a mind job.

clue.text: Nurse and medic treated disease

definitions.note: endemic is usually an adjective; as a noun it means an endemic disease

indicators.note: something treated has been worked on and altered, so these letters are processed into a new order

blocks.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hospital staff, a nurse and a doctor, cared for someone's illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' looks like the medical verb of the scene, but it signals the rearrangement of the doctor's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic is an illness constantly present within a particular region or population, such as malaria in some tropics.

clue.text: Simple one providing food without frills entertaining me, informally

indicators.note: frills are trimmings at the edges, so the word loses its outer letters
a host entertaining a guest has them inside the house, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a caterer supplies food
us is a colloquial way to say me, as in 'give us a kiss'

explanation.surface: A no-nonsense caterer serves plain fare to the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping the outer letters from the caterer leaves ATERE, and the informal 'me' goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere describes something plain and unadorned, a close synonym of simple in style.

clue.text: Pay women to get dates

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for women
dates and ages are both periods of time

explanation.surface: Someone pays women for romantic dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dates' suggests romance, but here it means periods of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Wages are the regular payment earned for work, a straightforward synonym of pay as a noun.

clue.text: 'Grand' and 'most ancient' describe wings of Christopher Wren?

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two outer edges, its first and last letters
to describe a circle is to draw round it, so these pieces go around another

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
the superlative of old
the outside letters of the first name

explanation.surface: Grand and ancient words are used of Sir Christopher Wren's architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Wren, architect of St Paul's, is split: his first name supplies outer letters while 'Wren' is the definition. The ? flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldcrest is a tiny songbird, like the wren, so a wren-like bird is offered as an example.

clue.text: Mostly screw, drinking sparkling wine: one could be at mine

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped
whoever is drinking takes the liquid inside, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: to screw money out of someone is to extort it
cava is a Spanish sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A drunken extortionist is at it again with the bubbly.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb meaning screw loses its last letter, then holds the Spanish fizz after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An excavator is a digging machine, so one may well be working at a quarry or pit.

clue.text: Charlie always put in credit card the other way round

indicators.note: whatever is put in goes inside, so these pieces are placed within the card

blocks.note: Visa is a brand of credit card
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: Charlie keeps sliding his credit card in back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other way round' sounds like a reversal signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice versa is the Latin phrase meaning with the order or positions reversed.

clue.text: Hurtful points in complaints

blocks.note: ill can mean harmful, as in ill effects
a ness is a headland or point of land

explanation.surface: Wounding remarks are made in a set of grievances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaints' reads as grievances, but it means ailments. A ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Inverness or Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints in the medical sense are ailments, the same as illnesses.

clue.text: Deal with kind public

blocks.note: a kind and a sort are both a type
once news is out it is public

explanation.surface: A thoughtful person handles the general public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like an adjective for gentle, but it is the noun meaning type.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort out a problem is to handle or resolve it, the phrasal equivalent of deal with.

clue.text: Pick up heavy breathing on microphone, that's shocking

indicators.note: to pick up is to hear and catch a sound, so the word is chosen for how it is heard

blocks.note: sighs are heavy breaths, and the word sounds like 'size'
the common short form

explanation.surface: A phone pest's heavy breathing is caught on the mic, which is shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' suggests a microphone or a phone, but it signals a sound-alike. The definition is extended: something seismic is earth-shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Seismic relates to earthquakes, figuratively anything with enormous impact, so a shock.

clue.text: Ford hybrid

blocks.note: first meaning: to wade across a river
second meaning: an animal or plant bred from two kinds

explanation.surface: A Ford car with a hybrid engine.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital F makes Ford look like the carmaker, but it is the verb to ford, to go across water.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for traversing a river and a noun for the offspring of two different breeds.

clue.text: Routine intruder? Inspector without lead to cross line

indicators.note: having no lead means the front letter is lost
a word stretched to cross something lies over it on both sides, enclosing it

blocks.note: a checker inspects things
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An inspector, leaderless, steps over a boundary while an intruder is about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Routine' means a comedian's act, not a daily habit, so the intruder is someone who interrupts a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A heckler shouts interruptions during a stand-up's act, intruding on the routine.

clue.text: Toilet: nothing is cleaner in bathroom?

blocks.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: Is there no cleaner for the bathroom toilet?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' suggests a person or a product like bleach, but it is a bath sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is the dried fibrous gourd used as a scrubbing sponge in the bath.

clue.text: Concerned with duke over Virginia: Queen stands by attacker

blocks.note: to be in something is to be involved or concerned with it
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state
D is the abbreviation for duke
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A duke presiding over Virginia, with the Queen supporting him, faces an assailant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' here means after: the duke follows Virginia. ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: An invader is one who attacks and enters territory by force, so an attacker.

clue.text: Daughter at store held up jeans

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means lifted so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
a mine is a store or rich supply

explanation.surface: A daughter at the shop holds up a pair of jeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Store' and 'held up' suggest a shop robbery; store is a rich source and the word is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is the cotton twill that jeans are made of, so it stands for the jeans themselves.

clue.text: Romeo and Juliet, both principally drunk bottle

indicators.note: principally means at the start, so each word keeps only its leading letter
someone drunk staggers about out of line, so these letters fall into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of each of these three words

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's lovers, both mainly tipsy, polish off a big bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is used whole, while 'principally' applies only to the three words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is an oversized wine or champagne bottle, holding about four standard bottles' worth.

clue.text: Wash back of woman in spring

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept
in places the one piece within the other

blocks.note: spring up and rise both mean to come up
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A woman washes her back in a natural spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' suggests water, matching the washing, but it is a verb meaning to rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash lightly with clean water, a direct synonym of wash.

clue.text: Fish in canal almost tricked to bite last of bait

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so that alone is taken
something tricked out is dressed up and remade, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fish in a canal was nearly fooled into taking the bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' looks like a deletion signal applied to canal, but it is part of the fodder letters. 'Fish' looks like a verb, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic salmon is a large migratory species of the North Atlantic, so a fish.
